results.name: Band Bench Press
instructions: Lie on a bench with your feet flat on the floor and place a resistance band under the bench, holding one handle in each hand. Bring your hands to shoulder height with your palms facing forward.
Press the handles upward until your arms are fully extended, keeping the band aligned with your arms.
Slowly lower the handles back to shoulder height with control, maintaining tension in the band.
Repeat the movement for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Ensure the resistance band is securely placed under the bench to avoid slipping.
Exhale as you press the band upward and inhale as you lower it back down.
Perform the exercise slowly and with control to maximize muscle engagement.
results.description: Band Bench Press is a beginner multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with a band, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Triceps, Shoulders.

results.name: Band Chest Fly
instructions: Secure the middle of the resistance band to a sturdy anchor point at head height. Stand facing away from the anchor point with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding one handle of the band in each hand.

Extend your arms out to the sides with a slight bend in your elbows, keeping your palms facing forward. Step forward to create tension in the band, positioning your hands slightly below shoulder height.
Move your arms in a wide arc motion, bringing your hands together in front of your chest. Squeeze your chest muscles as your hands meet, keeping a slight bend in your elbows throughout the movement.
Slowly return your arms to the starting position with control, maintaining tension in the band. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Ensure the resistance band is securely anchored to avoid slipping.
Exhale as you bring your hands together and inhale as you return to the starting position.
Focus on squeezing your chest muscles as you bring your hands together.
results.description: Band Chest Fly is a beginner single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with a band, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Biceps.

results.name: Band Cross Body One Arm Chest Press
instructions: Secure one end of the resistance band to a sturdy anchor point at chest height. Stand with your left side facing the anchor point and hold the handle of the band in your left hand, extending your arm out to the side with your elbow bent at 90 degrees.
Press the handle across your body to the right side, keeping your arm bent and in line with your chest until your hand reaches the opposite side of your body.
Slowly return your right arm back to the starting position, maintaining control and tension in the band.
Repeat the movement for the desired number of repetitions, then switch to the left arm.
tips: Ensure the resistance band is securely anchored to avoid slipping.
Exhale as you press the band across your body and inhale as you return to the starting position.
Focus on using your chest muscles to press the band.
results.description: Band Cross Body One Arm Chest Press is a beginner multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with a band, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Biceps.

results.name: Band High Fly
instructions: Secure the middle of the resistance band to a sturdy anchor point above head height. Stand facing away from the anchor point with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding one handle of the band in each hand.
Extend your arms out to the sides at shoulder height with a slight bend in your elbows, palms facing forward.
Move your arms in a wide arc motion, bringing your hands together in front of your chest. Squeeze your chest muscles as your hands meet, keeping a slight bend in your elbows throughout the movement.
Slowly return your arms to the starting position in the same wide arc motion. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Ensure the resistance band is securely anchored to avoid slipping.
Exhale as you bring your hands together and inhale as you return to the starting position.
Focus on squeezing your chest muscles as you bring your hands together.
results.description: Band High Fly is a beginner single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with a band, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Biceps.

results.name: Band Incline Bench Press
instructions: Adjust an incline bench to a 45-degree angle. Lie back on the bench with your feet on the floor, holding the band handles at shoulder height with your palms facing forward.
Press the handles upward until your arms are fully extended, keeping the band aligned over your chest.
Slowly lower the handles back to shoulder height with control, maintaining tension in the band.
Repeat the movement for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Ensure the resistance band is securely anchored under the bench to avoid slipping.
Exhale as you press the band handles upward and inhale as you lower them back down.
Perform the exercise slowly and with control to maximize muscle engagement.
results.description: Band Incline Bench Press is a beginner multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with a band, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Triceps.

results.name: Band Incline Fly
instructions: Adjust an incline bench to a 45-degree angle. Sit back on the bench with your feet flat on the floor. Place the resistance band under the bench and hold one handle of the band in each hand, extending your arms out to the sides with a slight bend in your elbows, palms facing up.
Engage your chest and bring the handles up in an arc motion towards each other until your hands meet above your chest.
Slowly return your arms to the starting position with control, maintaining the slight bend in your elbows.
Repeat the movement for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Ensure the resistance band is securely anchored under the bench to avoid slipping.
Exhale as you bring the handles together and inhale as you return to the starting position.
Use a resistance band with appropriate tension to ensure you can perform the exercise with good form.
results.description: Band Incline Fly is a beginner single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with a band, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Biceps.

results.name: Band Incline Hammer Press
instructions: Lie on an incline bench set at a 45-degree angle. Place the resistance band under the bench and hold one handle of the band in each hand with your palms facing each other, positioning your hands at chest height.
Press the handles upward until your arms are fully extended, keeping the band aligned over your chest.
Slowly lower the handles back to shoulder height with control, maintaining tension in the band.
Repeat the movement for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Ensure the resistance band is securely anchored under the bench to avoid slipping.
Exhale as you press the band handles upward and inhale as you lower them back down.
Avoid letting your elbows flare out excessively to protect your shoulder joints.
results.description: Band Incline Hammer Press is a beginner multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with a band, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Triceps.

results.name: Band Incline Palms Back Press
instructions: Lie on an incline bench set at a 45-degree angle with feet on the floor, holding one handle of the resistance band in each hand with your palms facing your chest, positioned at shoulder height.
Press the handles upward until your arms are fully extended, squeezing your chest muscles at the top of the movement.
Slowly lower the handles back to shoulder height with control.
Repeat for the desired repetitions.
tips: Ensure the resistance band is securely anchored under the bench to avoid slipping.
Use a resistance band with appropriate tension to ensure you can perform the exercise with good form.
Maintain a slight bend in your elbows at the top of the movement.
results.description: Band Incline Palms Back Press is a beginner multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with a band, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Triceps.

results.name: Band Low Alternate Chest Press
instructions: Secure the middle of the resistance band to a sturdy anchor point above head height. Step one foot in front and the other back, with both knees slightly bent, facing away of the anchor point, holding one handle of the band in each hand with your palms facing down, positioning your hands near to your shoulders.
Press the right handle forward until your arm is fully extended, keeping your left hand stationary.
Squeeze your chest muscles at the top of the movement, then slowly return the right handle to the starting position with control.
Repeat the pressing motion with your left hand, alternating between right and left arms for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Exhale as you press the band handle forward and inhale as you return it back.
Perform the exercise slowly and with control to maximize muscle engagement.
Avoid rotating your torso; keep your movements focused and controlled.
results.description: Band Low Alternate Chest Press is a beginner multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with a band, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Triceps.

results.name: Band Low Chest Fly
instructions: Secure the middle of the resistance band to a high anchor point above you. Step one foot in front and the other back, with both knees slightly bent, facing away from the anchor point, holding one handle of the band in each hand with your arms extended at your sides at shoulder level, palms facing forward.
Bring your arms down in a wide arc motion until your hands meet opposite your chest, keeping a slight bend in your elbows.
Squeeze your chest muscles at the top of the movement, then slowly raise your arms back to the starting position with control.
Repeat the fly motion for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep a slight bend in your elbows to protect your shoulder joints.
Focus on squeezing your chest muscles as you bring your hands together.
Use a resistance band with appropriate tension to ensure you can perform the exercise with good form.
results.description: Band Low Chest Fly is a beginner single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with a band, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Biceps.
